**Århus** is a Danish city and municipality located in the Central Denmark Region (Region Midtjylland) [^src1]. In the context of the Annual Report 2022–2023 for the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database (AFDK), Århus is evaluated at the municipal level to assess the clinical quality of care for patients with atrial fibrillation [^src1], [^src2]. It is important to note a point of disambiguation: the data refers strictly to the municipality of Århus within Region Midtjylland, rather than the broader region or the former Region Østjylland [^src1].

The AFDK report, prepared by the Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (RKKP), monitors key clinical indicators to benchmark healthcare outcomes across all 98 Danish municipalities [^src1], [^src2]. These include Indicator 5 (ischemic stroke) and Indicator 6 (intracranial hemorrhage), utilizing data primarily from the Danish National Patient Register (LPR) after the DanStroke registry was excluded due to system-related reporting issues [^src1]. For Århus, the municipal data for Indicator 5 shows that 43 out of 5,595 patients were registered with ischemic stroke, yielding a rate of 0.8% [^src1]. Additional tables covering Indicator 1 (early initiation of anticoagulation treatment) and further Indicator 5 metrics record 27 out of 5,592 patients at a 0.5% rate, alongside other treatment adherence benchmarks [^src2]. By breaking down these metrics at the municipal level, the report serves as a vital tool for local quality development and targeted healthcare improvements [^src2].
